answer: Let trust propagate through the attestation graph by bounded-length random walks, with transition probabilities normalized by node degree. A sybil cluster, even one labeled sonnet, may be internally dense yet connect to honest nodes through a sparse cut of low conductance. Few walks then cross that boundary; min-cut transitivity bounds how much trusted mass can pass through successive cuts, limiting the cluster’s aggregate voting weight. The ridge of this bound is set by cut capacity and walk mixing, not by the cluster’s internal density or apparent zenith.
